coverage_of_risk.rationale: No tests exist at all, and the riskiest logic (formatting, filtering, pagination, sorting, caching) is exactly the kind that unit tests would cover cheaply. Scored on what would be caught today: nothing.

findings.issue: apiFetch resolves any non-ok response (including transient 5xx) to null, and cached() memoizes resolved nulls for the process lifetime; one flaky API response permanently breaks that resource's page until restart. Nothing tests failure or cache-invalidation paths.
findings.suggestion: Only cache successful fetches (or delete the cache entry on null), and add unit tests for the cache: success memoization, rejection eviction, and 404-vs-500 handling.

findings.issue: The pure helpers encode the spec's trickiest formatting rules (mr-mime → 'Mr Mime', padStart(4), \s+ collapse of \n/\f flavor text, idFromUrl regex, '—' for missing) with no tests; a one-character regex or radix regression would silently corrupt every page.
findings.suggestion: Add a plain unit test file for format.ts — it has no dependencies and is the highest value-per-line test target in the repo.

findings.issue: Filtering (case-insensitive substring on humanized name, type/generation match), pagination math and page clamping are untested; off-by-one errors in the slice bounds or matching the wrong field would only be caught by slow e2e runs.
findings.suggestion: Extract the filter/paginate computation into a pure function and unit-test it: empty q, case insensitivity, combined filters, page clamp when results shrink, 48-per-page boundary.

findings.issue: The moves-table assembly — default game = highest version-group order, row dedup key, method ordering (level-up/machine/egg/tutor then alphabetical), default sort with MAX_SAFE_INTEGER for missing levels — is the app's most complex transformation and has no characterization tests.
findings.suggestion: Factor the row/table-building into a testable module and pin down: default game selection, method order, Level Up level-then-name ordering, and dedup behaviour.

findings.issue: compareRows/sortedRows implement missing-values-last-in-both-directions, numeric vs localeCompare ordering, and the ascending/descending toggle — pure logic that would be trivial to test but isn't.
findings.suggestion: Unit-test compareRows across all seven sort keys, both directions, and mixed missing values; also test the toggle direction-flip state transition.

findings.issue: Invalid URL params (bogus type/generation, non-numeric or out-of-range page) are silently coerced to defaults — a defined but untested behaviour; a future refactor could turn silent coercion into a crash or an unfiltered view.
findings.suggestion: Add tests for URL parsing edge cases: ?type=notatype, ?generation=bogus, ?page=0, ?page=abc, ?page=99999.

findings.issue: Unknown ?game= values fall back to the default game; this fallback path is untested and easy to break when touching the selection logic.
findings.suggestion: Test that ?game=nonexistent renders the default (highest-order) game rather than empty tables or a crash.

findings.issue: Alternate-form exclusion relies on the implicit invariant 'default pokemon id == species id, and forms (>10000) are absent from the species index', repeated across three pages via speciesById maps; nothing pins this invariant, so a data-layer refactor could reintroduce Mega forms into lists silently.
findings.suggestion: Extract a shared speciesFromPokemon helper and test it against fixtures including a form ID and a duplicate entry.

findings.issue: URL sync uses window.history.replaceState(window.history.state, ...), which is the correct Next App Router pattern, but back/forward and refresh-with-filters behaviour is unverified by the app.
findings.suggestion: Add one e2e-ish smoke test (or Playwright component test) asserting the URL after filter changes and after browser back.

findings.issue: No test script, runner, typecheck or lint script exists — there is no infrastructure for future tests to hang from, so the cost of adding tests later stays high.
findings.suggestion: Add a minimal setup now: 'test' script, vitest or playwright test, and a typecheck script, so early refactors are done against executable expectations.

summary: The app ships with zero tests of its own: no test files, no runner, and no test/typecheck script in package.json — every behaviour is guarded only by the externally-owned acceptance suite. The untested surface includes exactly the code most likely to rot: pure formatting helpers, filter/pagination logic, move-table sorting, and a memoizing data layer with a latent bug (transient API failures are cached as permanent not-founds). Unit-testing lib/format.ts, HomeBrowser's filtering, and the moves-table assembly would be cheap and would cover most of the real regression risk.
